快乐衣橱的衣服
 Clothes from the Happy Closet
dataList.description:
快乐衣橱送出的一套服装。把它交给弧光落地目灯吧。
 An outfit given by the Happy Closet. Let's hand it over to the Arc Floor Lamp.

从快乐衣橱的残骸中找到的一张碎纸片。上面写着“幸福”二字。它没有任何结构上的作用，却帮助快乐衣橱得以继续存在。
 A scrap of paper recovered from the remains of the Happy Closet. The word "Happiness" is written upon it. It served no structural purpose, yet it helped the Happy Closet to continue to exist.

赤红之神古老的“声音”再次响起，重复着它曾经诵念过的内容。这是赤红者们曾经听到过的“声音”。信仰越坚定的人，能听到的故事就越深邃。
 The Crimson God's old Voice plays again, repeating what it once recited. It is the Voice the Rouges once heard. Those of stronger faith could hear a more profound story.

dataList.description:
当光从裂缝中倾泻而出，触碰到每一个人时，百货商店里的人们开始变化。他们变成了自己所追求价值的形状，变成了自己所追随品牌所追求价值的形状。那些在变化中失去理智的人，被称为“人体模特”。但从本质上说，他们与我们其他人并无不同。
 When light spilled through the cracks and touched everyone, the people in the department store began to change. They took the shape of the values they pursued, the shape of the values pursued by the brands they followed. Those who lost their reason in the transformation came to be called Mannequins. In essence, however, they were no different from the rest of us.

一枚尖钉。尖钉能将目标固定在原地。没有锤子，就无法把它钉进去。可若是有人主动扑向尖钉，无论有没有锤子，都会把自己钉在原地。
 A nail. Nails fix their targets in place. Without a hammer, they cannot be driven in. Yet those who throw themselves upon a nail will pin themselves down, hammer or no hammer.

dataList.description:
你问改衣师是否应该保持中立？漆黑者偏爱布料，赤红者偏爱皮革。想想看，究竟哪个品牌更需要改衣师……她又更愿意把剪刀交给谁呢？
 You ask whether the Alterationist ought to remain neutral? The Noirs favor fabric, while the Rouges prefer hide. Think about it: which brand, then, needs the Alterationist more... and to whom will she be more willing to give her scissors?

 At Grand Magasin Sisyphe, food is not consumed for energy or survival. It is taken for one purpose alone: to sate the hunger of the heart.

牢笼让自由得以存在在在在在在。没有牢笼，自由便毫无意义义义义义义
 Cages bring freedom into beeeeeeing. Without cages, freedom is meaninglessssss

将那原始的脊椎，包裹进文明最崇高的材质之中，便造就了这枚金钉。
这根针能刺穿一切边界，从最卑微到最崇高。而后它会将其撕裂，落下眼泪。
 By sheathing the vertebrae, the primordial, in civilization's most exalted material, this Golden Nail was created.
This needle pierces every boundary, from the lowest to the highest. Then it tears.

衣服的种类繁多，但鞋子最为重要。它们是最先接触这个世界的衣物。
 Many kinds of clothing exist, but shoes matter most. They are the first garments that touch the world.

dataList.description:
鞋子需要呼吸。漆黑者的想法是错的——鞋履不该被密封起来。它们必须保持柔软，让双脚得以呼吸。唯有如此，你才能真正站立在大地之上。否则，你不过是被搁置于地面之上，与其下的土地隔绝而已。
 Shoes need to breathe. The Noirs have it wrong—footwear shouldn't be sealed shut. They need to stay supple and let the feet breathe. Only then can you truly stand upon the earth. Otherwise, you're merely laid upon it, cut off from the ground below.

dataList.description:
衣食住行。家具属于哪一类？它是人居住其中的东西，还是像衣服一样被穿在身上的东西？
哦，都不是。家具是衣物与居所之间的桥梁。
 Food, clothing, shelter. Where does furniture belong? Is it something we dwell in, or something we wear like clothing?
Oh, neither. Furniture is the bridge between clothing and shelter.

希望停止思考的顾客与员工，变成了西西弗百货里的家具。随后裂缝开始扩大，当那刺目的阳光倾泻而入、对他们低语时，家具便从沉睡中被撕扯出来，被迫开始行动。
 Customers and employees who wished to stop thinking became furnishings in Grand Magasin Sisyphe. Then the cracks began to widen, and when the fierce sunlight spilled through and whispered to them, the furnishings were torn from sleep and forced to move.

dataList.description:
一个可怜的赤红者曾问过，为什么我们要坐在桌前吃饭。为什么不干脆在地板上吃，何必这么麻烦？呵，仪式感会让食物变得更美味。经过艰辛与耐心才赢得的东西更甜美，因而也更有价值。照这个逻辑，桌椅越不舒适，用餐者就越文明。你不这么认为吗？
 A Rouge wretch once asked why we sit at a table to eat. Why go to such trouble instead of eating off the floor? Well, the ceremony makes food taste better. What is won through hardship and patience is sweeter, and therefore more valuable. By that logic, the more uncomfortable the table and chair, the more civilized the diner. Wouldn't you agree?

曾让快乐衣橱得以品尝滋味的器官。
 The organ that once allowed the Happy Closet to taste.

 The object that once allowed the Happy Closet to walk.

曾让快乐衣橱得以消化食物的器官。
 The organ that once allowed the Happy Closet to digest food.

曾让快乐衣橱得以见证世界之美的器官。
 The organ that once allowed the Happy Closet to behold the beauty of the world.

曾让快乐衣橱得以用表情流露情感的东西。
 That which once allowed the Happy Closet to reveal its feelings through expression.

曾让快乐衣橱的器官、骨骼、部件与肠子聚合并协同运作的机制。

针族侍奉着一位国王。这位国王是个美食家，他要求臣民不停地刺入。刺入是一把标尺，用美味在呻吟中的愉悦与痛苦中的尖叫来衡量价值。针族遵照国王的命令刺入，然后静静地舔舐渗出的分泌物。
 Needlekins serve a king. The king is a gourmet, and he demands that his subjects stab endlessly. Stabbing is a barometer that measures worth through the delicacy's moans of delight and screeches of pain. Needlekins stab as their king commands, and quietly lap up the secretions.

They see something they don't like? Stab! That's what they do. And when something oozes out, they lick it up. Glad I've got a thimble with me... I would've been in quite a pickle had I been caught down here without it.

一块摆放着各种染料的调色板。

那混合在一起的脓液味道，倒是相当缤纷多彩。
 A board on which dyes of many kinds are placed.

Basic colors are mixed upon it to create the desired shade. The right proportions and speed are essential to make what is wanted.

The smell of all that mingled pus is quite colorful.

要绘出丰富多彩的色谱，需要一支大刷子。刷子越小，自然笔触就越多，但笔触次数必须尽量控制到最少。刷子每点一下，都会在我身上留下泪珠，连同它的气味。

那气味让我哭泣，但我还是继续画。我为那个已经忘记眼泪与痛苦的人而画。
 One needs a large brush to paint a diverse spectrum of colors. Smaller brushes naturally lend themselves to more brushstrokes, but one must keep the number of strokes to a minimum. Each daub of the brush leaves tear droplets on me, and with them, its scent.

The scent makes me cry, but I keep painting. I paint for the one who has forgotten tears and pain.

味道，跟着悲伤的滋味走。

The flavor follows the taste of sorrow.

一把牙刷，刷头是一片细密尖钉组成的森林。

尖钉刮蹭皮肤，撕开并击穿嵌入其中的东西，将皮下的体液排出。

然后，把它呈给国王品尝。
 A toothbrush whose head is a forest of spindly nails.

The nails grate the skin, ripping and breaking through what is embedded. This drains the subdermal fluid.

Then, it is brought to the king for tasting.

正午时分，太阳升至最高点。太阳越高，影子越短。当阳光变为蓝色时，影子会缩短到肉眼不可见。
 At noon, the sun reaches its highest point. The higher the sun, the shorter the shadow. The shadow shrinks beyond sight when the sunlight is blue.

dataList.description:

 This dish grants the complete experience of being eaten. Tasting it brings death, for the taster has become consumed as prey.

那茧像是在呼唤着谁一样哭泣着。这个孩子从一段早已逝去的过去被带来，随波逐流冲上岸，一路漂到了美食广场……如今已经变成了一道菜。
 The cocoon cries as if calling out to someone. Carried from a past now gone, the child washed ashore, drifted as far as the Food Court... and has now become a dish.

dataList.description:
看不见的东西，必须被颜色反复覆盖，直到轮廓浮现出来。把足够多的颜色泼洒在那些看不见的东西上，你就会意识到自己的躯干也已经被染上了颜色。
 What is invisible must be coated in color until its outline emerges. Splash enough unseen things with color, and one realizes that one's own body has become stained.

每隔很长一段时间，就会有一滴眼泪从最深处被打捞出来，浮肿不堪。经过一段漫长而艰辛的搅拌，去除那股恶臭与黑污之后……这滴眼泪才恢复原本的澄澈。

深海染料，正是用这类古老存在的眼泪制成的。
 There is a tear that, once every long while, is dredged up bloated from the deepest depths. After a long, grueling process of stirring through the rancid stench and the smudging black... the tear regains its original clarity.

The Deep-sea Dye is made from the tears of such olden beings.

将金色树脂分泌的液体与脓液混合。

每一分金色都密密实实地饱含着意义与价值，足以让任何染料同样染上金色。困难的部分在于如何获取那分泌物。
 Mix the secretion from the Golden Resin with the pus.

Each ounce of the golden is densely saturated with meaning and worth, enough to turn any dye just as aureate. The hard part is getting the secretion.

为了运输而缠绕起来的织线。转啊，转啊，转啊……在它生命的每一个阶段，这根线都在旋转。
 Woven threads wound for transport. Spin, spin, spin... In every step of its life, the thread spins.

眼泪如黄色的脓液般涌出。
 Tears well like yellow pus.

那红肿的眼泪，像一个满是脓液的脓包一样破裂开来。
 The red, swollen tears burst like a pus-filled abscess.

蓝色染料闻起来有脓液的气味。
 The blue dye smells of pus.

人为什么会在黑暗中摸索，去寻找意义的碎屑？
意义究竟是碎屑本身固有的，还是这寻找的过程本身，才赋予了它意义？
 Why does one stumble in the dark for the crumbs of meaning?
Does one find meaning inherent in the crumbs, or does the search itself imbue them with one?

你知道食物到哪里为止算是食物，从哪里开始算是残渣吗？

咬一口就把剩下的扔掉，那就成了废物。可对某些人来说，那废物却成了绝佳的稀有食材，被欣喜地吞下。我的意思是，在美食广场里，什么才算残渣，是一个极其重要的问题……而眼下，任何不是漆黑者的东西都被当成了残渣。
 Do you know where food ends and scraps begin?

Take one bite and throw the rest away, and it becomes refuse. But to some, that waste becomes a wonderfully rare ingredient, devoured with delight. What I mean is, what counts as scraps is an incredibly important issue in the Food Court... and right now, anything that isn't Noir is considered scraps.

而它，落入了赤红者手中。

dataList.description: 鞋子还需要袜子，这事挺奇怪的。我们穿鞋是为了保护双脚，可为什么还要在脚和鞋之间再垫一层，来保护这两者？ 又或者……那份多余，正是袜子尊严的来源。鞋子属于本能——我们需要鞋子，是因为没有它脚会疼；而袜子属于文明的范畴，因为我们想要那份舒适。 It's strange that shoes require socks. We wear shoes to protect our feet, yet we place another layer between the foot and the shoe to protect them both? Or... perhaps that excess is what gives socks their dignity. Shoes belong to instinct—we need shoes because our feet hurt without them, while socks fall within the realm of civilization because we want the comfort.

dataList.description:
赤红者的品牌总监。

品牌的每一层意义与方向，都是在她的号令下确定的。没有人比她更清楚地听见过赤红之神的“声音”。令人钦佩的是，即使在那“声音”消失之后，这位品牌总监仍然试图塑造一个新的存在，好让那“声音”能够再次被听见。若她愿意，赤红之神的缺席本可以一直被隐瞒下去，但她选择了不这么做。
 Le Rouge's Brand Director.

Every meaning and direction of the brand was decided under her command. No one heard the Crimson God's Voice more clearly than she did. Admirably, even after that Voice vanished, the Brand Director sought to fashion a new being through which the Voice might be heard again. The Crimson God's absence could have remained hidden had she wished it so, but she chose not to.
